value.title: Stop tool-list flips on proxied Copilot seats; weigh per-seat TTL
value.summary: Evidence plan for workstream 004 s07. A canary confirms that toolSearch=false (applied user-wide by the prime on Jordan's go, not code here) holds the proxied tool list flat. sim232.py re-prices egret's windows with the flips gone, and finds that a per-seat TTL doesn't pay, so every seat keeps 1h. Docs and sim scripts only.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: On proxied (BYOK) Copilot seats, Copilot 1.0.114's client-side generic tool search leaves deferred tools out of the tools array until they are activated, then drops them again. availableToolCount swung between 30 and 50, and tools lead the cached prefix, so every swing re-wrote the whole prompt at the 1-hour price: 87% of hot flips re-wrote more than half the prompt, and egret's survey put 35% of proxied spend on them. The fix is a setting, not code. `toolSearch: false` cannot be set from a repo, so the prime applied it user-wide in ~/.copilot/settings.json on Jordan's go at 2026-11-19T03:27:46Z; this PR contains none of it. This plan proves the fix on a canary, measures its price (a larger tool prefix), and re-prices the fleet with the flips gone by extending egret's sim.py. It also weighs a per-seat cache TTL in the proxy. That doesn't pay, so every seat keeps 1h and nothing is built.

sections.name: goals
value: Proxied seats keep a fixed tool list, so a hot turn reads its prompt from cache instead of re-writing it.
The fleet's cost with the fix is known in egret's terms: against plain, against the proxy as it ran, and part by part.
The per-seat TTL question is answered with numbers and closed.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No proxy, daemon or CLI code. The fix is a Copilot setting the prime applied user-wide; this PR only documents and measures it.
No fix for the extensions_reload token-only flip (a known residual, below).
No change to the shared sidecar, its config or LaunchAgent, or the prod daemon.
No per-request TTL mix: takin's spike showed a 1h marker read over a 5m entry never upgrades it.

value.claim: A proxied Copilot seat started after the setting keeps availableToolCount flat through bash calls, an async shell with read_bash, extensions_reload and user turns: 0 count flips, and hot follow-ups write under 1% of the prompt. Known residual: an extensions_reload can change toolTokenCount with the count unchanged and re-write the prompt once (1 of 2 reloads on the canary).
The fix's price is measured, not assumed: tool definitions grow from 17,913 to 30,846 tokens (+12,933) on every request. The sim prices that growth as reads on a cache hit and as writes on a miss.

sim232.py re-prices egret's two windows as proxied-fixed beside plain and proxied, with each token class at its own record's listed price, which sums to billed exactly. It also shows the flip removal and the prefix growth on their own.

Per-seat TTL policies are weighed against 1h for all and 5m for all on the fixed regime, under the never-upgrade rule. The verdict is recorded, and proxy code is built only on a clear win (none: every seat keeps 1h).

The live after-window is reported split by Copilot process start (before or after 03:27:46Z), with a dated receipt at 03:40Z, then re-run once with at least an hour of post-restart data before the round-1 verdicts.
Workstream 004 gains s07, which delivers req-01 and req-07 and names this plan. Its changelog row says the fix was applied user-wide by the prime on Jordan's go and is not code in this PR.

value.title: Canary, sim and verdict recorded
value.brief: One PR: plan, evidence scripts and their outputs under assets/, workstream 004 s07. No code.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Cause (pm-004, confirmed by the prime). On the BYOK Anthropic route, Copilot 1.0.114 runs client-side generic tool search (flag copilot_cli_tool_search_client_generic). Deferred tools stay out of the tools array until activated and are dropped again afterwards (copilot_cli_tool_deferral_sticky null). A bash call adds the 5 async-shell companions, and extensions_reload adds 1 or removes 5. On CAPI, hosted tool search keeps the array fixed. Setting scope: `copilot config --local toolSearch false` refuses, because toolSearch is not among the settings a repo may override, and neither a flag nor an env var sets it. Copilot reads settings.json only at process start, so seats started before 03:27:46Z keep flipping until restarted. Canary (assets/canary-sessions.md): proxied opus 23fd00ea held 49 tools on all 18 requests, and its hot writes were 96-423 tokens (0.2-0.9%). The first extensions_reload changed toolTokenCount from 30,846 to 36,528 and back with the count unchanged, costing one full re-write (48,911) and a 20.6% one. The second reload changed nothing. The prime's haiku canary e6499e1f held 49 over 5 requests. Price of the fix: fresh opus seats used to write about 17-22k of a 37-43k prompt and read about 20k of prefix that other seats had already cached. After the change, b7d8d616 wrote 16,744 of 51,162 and read 34,418 from that shared prefix. Restart cost: the first request after a restart re-writes the whole prompt once (7c8a587b: 300,980 of 335,398), so a rolling restart costs one full 1h write per seat. Sim (assets/sim232.md, egret's method): proxied-fixed against plain comes to +25.7% saving before #243 and +6.9% after, where the proxy as it ran was -10.7% and -27.6%. Opus <5 min costs 26.4 AIU/1M against plain's 22.5; 5-60 min costs 82.9 against 414.9 (a thin cell, n=103). The larger prefix alone costs about 1.5 points. A mechanistic segment-cache sim lands within +5.3% of billed for the proxied sessions as they ran; removing the flips cuts it by 29%, or 24% with the prefix growth. Per-seat TTL: against 1h for all, every buildable policy costs 6-26% more, and even a per-seat hindsight bound saves only 0.9-3.8%. Once a seat drops to 5m, its prefix stays 5m until the next full miss.

value.risk: The before-window saving rests on a thin proxied 5-60 min cell (n=103).
value.mitigation: The mechanistic sim, calibrated to billed within 5.3%, gives the same direction. The live after-window is re-run as data accrues.

value.risk: Seats started before 03:27:46Z keep flipping until restarted, and each restart re-writes its whole prompt once.
value.mitigation: Restarts are the prime's rollout. The after-window is split by process start so old seats don't mask the gain.

value.risk: extensions_reload can still bust the cache (a token-only flip).
value.mitigation: Recorded as a known residual. flip_window.py counts toolTokenCount changes, so it stays visible.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Worktree fleet-232-proxy-tool-flips, branch coder/232-proxy-tool-flips; edits by absolute path.
Usage fields only: no session text, no credential files, no tokens in outputs. Scripts read $HOME, with no hard-coded user paths.
Never change ~/.copilot/settings.json or shared repo settings; the live seats are only the canary this plan spawned.
